description: Change a .tscn safely, without the editor: add a node (a Godot class or an instanced scene), remove a node (with its children, connections and the resources only it used), set a property (name and type checked against Godot 4.7; enums by name, resources as res:// files), connect or disconnect a signal (checks the signal exists, and warns when the method is missing or takes the wrong number of arguments, with the func line to add), or attach a script (refuses one that extends another node type). Node paths are relative to the scene root, which is ".". `op` picks the change and which fields it needs: add_node (parent, name, and type or instance), remove_node (node), set (node, property, value), connect and disconnect (from, signal, to, method), attach_script (node, script). Only the lines of that change are touched. Without `write` it changes nothing and returns the diff and warnings; with `write: true` it writes and reports the review errors before and after (an error result when there are more after). A missing field or a change it refuses returns an error and writes nothing. Use it instead of editing .tscn files by hand. For project.godot use godot_project_edit; to rename a node everywhere, use godot_rename.

from.description: connect/disconnect: path of the node that emits

instance.description: add_node: a res:// scene to instance instead of a type

name.description: add_node: name of the new node

node.description: remove_node/set/attach_script: path of the node ("." is the root)

parent.description: add_node: path of the parent ("." is the root)

scene.description: the scene: res://main.tscn, or a path

script.description: attach_script: res:// path of the script

to.description: connect/disconnect: path of the node that receives

type.description: add_node: a Godot node class, e.g. Sprite2D

value.description: set: the value, e.g. Vector2(10, 20), 3, true, ALWAYS, res://icon.svg, null

write.description: write the change (default false: show the diff only)

name: godot_scene_edit
title: Change a scene
